title: IAM provisioning and role governance review with Aperture Health
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 Type II and ISO summary link (Maya) by 2026-03-24
Engineering-only SCIM attribute-mapping session with Carlos and Ravi scheduled (tentative) 2026-03-29
Provision a short pilot org in Redwood Dedicated for Aperture test tenant (Priya to follow up) by 2026-04-02
action_items: Maya: Send security pack + SOC2 PDF + ISO checklist (due 2026-03-24)
Carlos: Prepare SCIM mapping template and example group filters, include example SCIM patch flows (due 2026-03-26)
Ravi: Provide existing IdP SAML attribute list and current role hierarchy doc (due 2026-03-25)
Mei: Share current audit log retention policy and any compliance controls (due 2026-03-28)
meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-22 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Lena Ortiz (Aperture Head Eng), Dr. Sameer Patel (Aperture CISO), Ravi Kumar (IAM), Mei Wong (DevOps)
summary: High-level review of SAML SSO setup, SCIM provisioning expectations, and RBAC / least-privilege model for Aperture Health. Customer strongly focused on audit trails, key management for encryption, and EU data residency for certain PHI-adjacent telemetry. Agreed to run a short Dedicated pilot and a follow-up engineering workshop for attribute mapping.
topics: SCIM group sync and provisioning semantics
RBAC patterns: role vs permission vs group
Audit logs, retention and export for e-discovery
SOC 2 / ISO evidence and attestation cadence
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining. Uh quick roll call, and we'll jump into the SSO and RBAC bits. 
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: Hi, Lena here. Sorry joining from SF, noise in background. 
[00:17] Dr. Sameer Patel: Sameer on the call. Our timeline is pretty tight, looking to finalize decision by end of Q2. 
[00:22] Maya Chen: Great — we can go over SAML setup, SCIM flows, and then role models. Carlos will cover the technical mapping. 
[00:30] Carlos Rivera: Hey all. Quick note, I'll reference the attribute map doc I emailed earlier, um there might be a couple typos in the example claims — the "mail" vs "email" mapping often trips folks. 
[00:45] Ravi Kumar: One thing we need is group sync. We currently rely on groups in Okta to express department and compliance tier. We need SCIM to handle group membership changes fast, and also deprovisioning within 5 minutes ideally.
[01:02] Carlos Rivera: Right, so Redwood supports group push via SCIM v2; there are two modes — full sync and delta patch. Delta patch should meet that 5 to 10 minute window, although network latency to the Dedicated node in eu-west can add seconds. 
[01:22] Mei Wong: Are we talking about Hosted or Dedicated? For PHI-adjacent logs we need them to stay in the EU region. 
[01:28] Maya Chen: Good call. For data residency you can use Redwood Dedicated deployed in your VPC or Redwood Private. Dedicated keeps inference and audit logs in the chosen region; Private is for air-gapped on-prem. For this pilot we suggested a Dedicated node in eu-west-1. 
[01:45] Dr. Sameer Patel: We need to confirm encryption at rest keys — can we integrate with our KMS? We don't want Redwood managing keys directly. 
[01:53] Carlos Rivera: Yes, we have KMS integrations. For Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and HSM-backed solutions. There is a configuration endpoint in the control plane to point to CMK. Note: the control plane metadata still flows through Redwood console unless you're on Private; we'll clarify that in the security pack. 
[02:15] Lena Ortiz: Ok, also curious about audit logs. We need immutable logs for all administrative actions and token issuance, with export to our SIEM. 
[02:24] Priya Nair: We can ship audit logs via secure syslog and S3 exports. Logs include admin activity, role changes, and SCIM provisioning events. Retention is configurable; default retention in Hosted is 90 days but Dedicated can be configured to 7 years in line with your policy. 
[02:40] Ravi Kumar: Can Redwood provide a streaming endpoint to attach to our Splunk? 
[02:44] Carlos Rivera: Yes, we expose a streaming webhook and S3 export. There are also incremental log hooks for real-time alerts. Small caveat: if you choose the hosted control plane, some metadata for provisioning orchestration crosses regions for resilience — which matters if you have strict data locality regs. 
[03:02] Dr. Sameer Patel: That cross-region metadata point — can you quantify what metadata? Usernames, group ids? We need to know if anything PHI-pseudonymized leaves region. 
[03:14] Carlos Rivera: Very fair. In Dedicated, the payload is minimized to IDs, timestamps, and orchestration state. We will include field-level list in the security pack. 
[03:25] Lena Ortiz: On RBAC, our model today is role-based with a handful of top-level roles: viewer, clinician, researcher, admin. But we also have attribute-based restrictions — like data access flags per dataset. How do we layer that in? 
[03:40] Carlos Rivera: You can use Redwood's role model mapped to groups via SCIM, and then do dataset-level entitlements via route-level ACLs. There's an ability to pass custom claims from SAML into the session token which the runtime enforces. Note: sometimes the claim gets mangled if the IdP uses urn:oid attributes; mapping is important. 
[04:05] Ravi Kumar: For least-privilege, we prefer a roles + permission set approach vs wide groups. How is role inheritance handled? 
[04:12] Carlos Rivera: Redwood supports hierarchical roles — e.g., admin > clinician > viewer — and explicit deny rules. The more common pattern we see in healthcare is to keep narrow roles and use group-scoped permissions for dataset bindings. That reduces blast radius. 
[04:28] Mei Wong: In practice we want automatic deprovisioning on offboarding. If someone leaves, the SCIM delete event must fully revoke tokens and remove KV-cache entries — sorry, KV cache — I mean KV cache. 
[04:41] Carlos Rivera: Right, we have webhook hooks for session invalidation and token revocation. There is a short TTL for unauthenticated sessions but for long-lived API keys we recommend rotation and audit hooks. 
[04:55] Dr. Sameer Patel: About key rotation — if we use our KMS, does Redwood rotate on our behalf or do we keep the rotation lifecycle? 
[05:03] Maya Chen: If you bring your CMK, you control rotation policies. Redwood can trigger re-encryption events but does not rotate your customer-managed key in KMS. We'll document the operational steps. 
[05:15] Lena Ortiz: Ok. Another ask — can we get an export of all role assignments for quarterly audit? Prefer CSV and time-stamped. 
[05:23] Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood provides a role assignment export. We can also schedule automated exports to your S3 with encryption and access logs enabled. 
[05:33] Ravi Kumar: On SAML specifics — mapping groups to roles: do we need to push groups or do you recommend claim-based mapping? 
[05:41] Carlos Rivera: Both work. Claim-based mapping is simpler for static assignments, but group push via SCIM gives you live membership and deprovisioning. For dynamic membership changes SCIM delta is better. 
[05:55] Lena Ortiz: If SCIM is misconfigured and creates duplicate users, what's the remediation path? 
[06:01] Carlos Rivera: We have reconciliation APIs and manual merge flows; also a conflict policy flag that determines whether SCIM PATCH will merge or fail on conflicts. We usually recommend fail-safe during pilot. 
[06:15] Dr. Sameer Patel: Are there limits on SCIM throughput? We expect bulk provisioning during onboarding. 
[06:21] Carlos Rivera: There are rate limits on Hosted but Dedicated can be scaled. For a bulk import we suggest using the admin CSV import to avoid spiky SCIM calls. We'll include recommended batch sizes. 
[06:34] Maya Chen: Quick pivot — competitors and legacy concerns? 
[06:36] Lena Ortiz: We've evaluated CloudVendorX and also looked at building in-house with LlamaStack; CloudVendorX had tighter native Okta integration but costs more. 
[06:46] Carlos Rivera: Ok noted. We'll highlight differences in the security pack. 
[06:50] Ravi Kumar: For the audit trail, can we get cryptographic signing of logs? 
[06:54] Carlos Rivera: We support optional signing with HSM-backed key for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we sign logs at ingestion with our service key but you can request signed exports. 
[07:06] Mei Wong: Minor transcription glitch — sometimes product names come through odd in the call exports. 
[07:09] Maya Chen: Haha yes. 
[07:14] Maya Chen: Next, a really practical piece — attribute mapping table. Carlos, can you walk us through a simple example for Okta -> Redwood? 
[07:22] Carlos Rivera: Sure. Example: Okta SAML assertion containing NameID (email), attribute 'groups' as array, and custom 'x-data-access' claim. You'd map NameID to principal.email, groups to principal.groups, and x-data-access to session.claims.data_access. In some IdPs the groups list is emitted as a string; we'll show how to parse. 
[07:45] Ravi Kumar: We currently send groups as a comma separated string; is there a recommended change? 
[07:49] Carlos Rivera: Ideally emit as array, but we can transform on the Redwood side with a small mapping script. That is something Carlos will demo in the follow-up engineering session. 
[08:02] Lena Ortiz: Great. On the least-privilege discussion, can we enforce mandatory MFA for admin role only? 
[08:08] Carlos Rivera: Yes, role-based MFA is supported and enforced at authentication time. You can also require step-up for sensitive endpoints. 
[08:16] Dr. Sameer Patel: What about session lifetime controls for researchers vs clinicians? Researchers should have shorter session TTL. 
[08:22] Carlos Rivera: Per-role session TTL is supported. We'll include sample policies. 
[08:29] Mei Wong: One more point — e-discovery. We may need to pull all actions for a subject for legal holds. How easy is it? 
[08:36] Priya Nair: We can run export queries against the audit store; we also expose an API to pull events for a given principal id. Exports are signed and can be time-bounded. 
[08:47] Lena Ortiz: Back to compliance — SOC2 evidence. We will need periodic attestations and access to control mappings. 
[08:54] Maya Chen: We'll share SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO 27001 summary. For customer audits we provide a SOC2 bridge letter and an audit contact to coordinate evidence transfer. 
[09:07] Dr. Sameer Patel: For the record, please include any third-party subprocessors and locations. Also whether subprocessor list changes trigger notifications. 
[09:16] Maya Chen: Yes, that's standard. Subprocessor list and notification cadence are in the compliance pack. 
[09:21] Ravi Kumar: Practical question — how does role rollback work if someone is mistakenly promoted to admin? 
[09:26] Carlos Rivera: There's an admin review workflow and an automated approval queue. We can set a two-person approval for privilege escalation. There's also an audit event that triggers alerts for new admin grants. 
[09:40] Mei Wong: We'll want to test privileged access with a simulated phish/breach scenario. Is there a breakglass flow? 
[09:47] Carlos Rivera: Yes, breakglass with timeboxed elevated tokens is available and recorded in the audit log.
[09:55] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. What's the recommended pilot scope? 
[10:00] Maya Chen: For a short pilot: 50 users, SCIM delta provisioning, Okta SAML, role mapping for clinician/researcher/viewer, KMS with CMK in eu-west, audit export to your S3. Duration 2 weeks. 
[10:13] Ravi Kumar: That timeline could work. We'll need a list of required IdP metadata fields. 
[10:17] Carlos Rivera: I'll send a checklist in the mapping template. 
[10:20] Maya Chen: Cool. Any final security blockers? 
[10:23] Dr. Sameer Patel: Only that we need to review the detailed field-level data flows. Also confirm that telemetry doesn't include PHI. 
[10:31] Carlos Rivera: Telemetry is anonymized by default; raw request payloads containing sensitive text are not persisted in Hosted, and in Dedicated we recommend disabling request-level logging or routing them to customer-controlled stores. We'll document the exact flags. 
[10:45] Lena Ortiz: Ok let's wrap. Thanks everyone. 
[10:48] Maya Chen: Recap: We'll send SOC2/ISO pack, SCIM mapping template, schedule engineering attribute workshop, and spin up a Dedicated pilot. Next calls: engineering-only 2026-03-29 tentative. 
[10:58] Dr. Sameer Patel: Thanks, appreciate it. 
[11:00] Meeting ends — 46 minutes
notes: Customer emphasized data residency, KMS, and fast deprovision. Agreed pilot scope and deliverables. Some idp naming mismatches expected; follow-on mapping session required.
